reading.body:
Business interruption insurance now covers the AI stack end to end, from utility load shedding and drought water shutoffs to hyperscaler outages and model API failures.

The pattern is that most of these ten coverages are contingent. The loss is triggered by someone else's failure: a utility throttling supply, a cloud region going dark, a cable severed at sea, an independent power producer missing its delivery date, a municipality cutting cooling water, a third party model API going unavailable. Only edge node update corruption reads as a first party operational failure. AI downtime is being underwritten as a dependency problem, not an internal reliability problem.

Four of the ten are directly about power or water: load shedding and throttling, power purchase agreement failure, drought related water shutoffs, and interconnection queue delay. That is the physical constraint on AI scaling appearing in an insurance product list. A stalled interconnection queue or a failed megawatt delivery is treated as an insurable interruption, which means the risk of not getting power on schedule is now priced alongside the risk of losing it.

What this does not tell you is whether any of it has happened. There are no premiums, no limits, no claim counts, no carriers, and no loss amounts. A taxonomy of coverage categories is evidence that insurers see these exposures, not evidence that they have paid out on them. The list also says nothing about which of these risks is largest, or whether the products are actually sold rather than merely drafted.
